issues.title: [llemy] [llemy-test] Create hello.txt with "hello world"
issues.body:
# Implementation Plan

## Objective
- A file `hello.txt` exists at the repo root containing exactly the text `hello world`

## Non-goals
- No subdirectory creation
- No additional content or formatting in the file

## Files to change
**New:**
- `hello.txt`

**Modify:**
- None

## Commands
- **lint:** None
- **test:** None
- **build/typecheck:** None

## Interfaces / I/O
- File content must be exactly: `hello world` (no trailing newline or extra characters)

## Behaviour rules / Edge cases
- If `hello.txt` already exists, overwrite it with the exact content

## Acceptance checklist
- [ ] `hello.txt` exists at the repo root
- [ ] File content is exactly `hello world`
- [ ] No extra whitespace, newlines, or characters beyond `hello world`

## Assumptions
- "hello world" means the literal string without a trailing newline

## Stop conditions
- `hello.txt` exists at repo root with exact content `hello world`

## Workflow instructions for Codex
For every `llemy-todo` issue:
- Work on current branch
- Implement the issue exactly as written
- Do not commit all changes
- Do not push the branch to origin
- Add a completion comment summarising changes
- Label the issue `llemy-done` and remove `llemy-todo`
- Do not merge
- Do not use sandbox CLI - always use the real `gh` CLI tool
